
## User outcome
Turn the current static ARQ public site into a distinctive editorial-technical system without weakening its strongest properties: static HTML, no client-side JavaScript, no third-party requests, governed claims, accessibility, dark appearance, 320px support and 200% zoom.

## Current evidence / known gap
The current `apps/marketing` implementation is structurally sound but visually repetitive. It relies on one 68rem measure, a conventional hero scale and a small shared component vocabulary. `design/page-renderings/PAGE-RENDERINGS-MANIFEST.csv` still marks public visual assets as deferred. Marketing CSS also duplicates canonical brand colour values and currently uses a different dark green than `design/tokens/brand.v4.css`. `layout.ts` hardcodes a stale `REV B · 2026-08` footer label.

## First implementation slice
1. Preserve the current integration authority from #332. Do not assume `main`.
2. Add the approved master public-site plan to the repository.
3. Establish a canonical brand-token bridge for marketing without creating a second brand authority.
4. Remove the stale hand-maintained revision month.
5. Add an additive editorial CSS layer rather than destabilising the existing stylesheet in one large rewrite.
6. Add typed shared editorial primitives needed for PUB-001.
7. Recompose PUB-001 using governed current copy and explicit current/limit state pairs.
8. Preserve all public-site route, language, claim, accessibility and no-external-resource invariants.
9. Open a PR and use CI as the executable evidence layer available to this lane.

## Owned files for this slice
Primary ownership:
- `docs/design/ARQ-PUBLIC-WEBSITE-EDITORIAL-SYSTEM-MASTER-PLAN-v1.0.md`
- `apps/marketing/src/layout.ts`
- `apps/marketing/src/build.ts`
- `apps/marketing/src/editorial.css` (new)
- `apps/marketing/src/components.ts`
- `apps/marketing/src/content/home.ts`
- focused public-site tests only if required by the implementation

Do not overlap another active lane touching these files without reconciliation.

## Non-negotiables
- no framework rewrite;
- no client JS dependency for core content;
- no external resources;
- no fake product screenshots, metrics or capability;
- no weakening ARQ Language System 4.1;
- no second semantic capability vocabulary;
- `.arq opens` must stay adjacent to `does not save back`;
- 3D viewing must not become 3D authoring by implication;
- state cannot rely on colour alone;
- mobile/200% zoom/accessibility outrank exact visual mimicry;
- do not change the public route contract as part of styling work.

## Evidence required before completion
- exact branch head;
- CI/build/type/test status on that head;
- public-site language/claim checks;
- no-external-resource checks;
- responsive/zoom/visual evidence where current tooling can produce it;
- explicit report of any evidence that remains not-inspected rather than treating it as green.

## Completion boundary
This issue is not the entire 17-page rollout. The first closeable checkpoint is a verified shared foundation plus PUB-001 visual proof. PUB-002 onward should proceed only after that system is proven and reviewed.

- define one canonical tolerance ladder with purpose-specific fields rather than one global epsilon;
- distinguish at minimum coordinate coincidence, zero-length/degeneracy, intersection/topology, angle, area, snap/display and import/reconciliation tolerances where the architecture requires separate semantics;
- define how tolerances scale or do not scale with canonical units, world extents and view-space interactions;
- measure behaviour on representative architectural extents and adversarial fixtures, including very small details, large site coordinates, near-parallel segments, nearly coincident endpoints, repeated transforms and import round trips;
- document which tolerances are model-semantic and which are UI/view-space only;
- update all Core geometry/operation consumers to use the accepted named policy;
- add a check for forbidden stray model-space epsilons outside explicitly approved modules;
- define compatibility/migration consequences if tolerance changes affect derived topology or validation in existing projects.

## Out of scope
Do not choose the canonical numeric representation here. Do not hide algorithm instability by simply increasing tolerances until tests pass. Do not make screen-pixel snap tolerance a canonical geometric truth.

## Safety rules
- invalid/ambiguous geometry must fail explicitly rather than being coerced into coincidence;
- tolerance changes must not silently rewrite persisted canonical coordinates;
- imported geometry reconciliation must report any approximation that crosses material fidelity boundaries;
- topology-changing tolerance changes require explicit compatibility review.

## Evidence
Benchmark/fixture matrix across representative scales; property/adversarial tests; import/export round trips; wall join/room boundary/dimension reference regression suite; repeated-edit drift tests; exact-head performance measurement.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] #88 is resolved first or this issue remains blocked.
- [ ] One documented named tolerance ladder is accepted and used by Core model operations.
- [ ] No unapproved model-space magic epsilons remain in the scoped packages.
- [ ] Screen/view tolerances are clearly separated from semantic geometry tolerances.
- [ ] Wall joins, room boundaries, stable references and supported import reconciliation pass calibrated adversarial fixtures.
- [ ] Existing project compatibility effects are measured and documented.
- [ ] Changing a tolerance requires targeted evidence and cannot silently weaken validation globally.

## ZEUS CTO reconciliation
#369 must review this together with #88, wall/room/dimension lanes and import adapters because a tolerance change can produce cross-cutting semantic regressions even when each package's unit tests remain green.

## User outcome
When local browser storage is constrained, ARQ warns early, explains the difference between working-copy risk and published-file safety, and fails writes predictably without pretending work is durable.

## In scope
- measure available storage where the platform permits it, without treating estimates as guarantees;
- define thresholds for warning/critical states using measured project/resource size;
- distinguish canonical working-copy bytes, recoverable journal/metadata and disposable derived caches;

Persistent but non-blocking warning before critical pressure; blocking error only when a required write cannot be acknowledged. Never show `saved` after quota failure. Provide a clear next action and current risk state.

## Safety
Never delete canonical project data automatically to satisfy quota. Do not promise exact free-space values when browser APIs only provide estimates.

## Evidence
Injected quota/error tests, large project/resource fixtures, cache eviction tests, browser capability checks, restart/recovery after failed writes.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Quota/write failures produce honest unsaved state.
- [ ] Disposable caches can be reclaimed without changing semantic project state.
- [ ] Canonical data is never auto-deleted for space.
- [ ] Warnings/actions match platform capabilities.

## Objective

Make every ARQ implementation lane self-contained enough that an agent can safely pick one issue, understand the user outcome, identify dependencies/conflicts, implement it, prove it, update the issue, and hand it back without relying on hidden chat context.

This issue does **not** replace #317/#319. It builds the programme-level issue contract on top of their ownership protocol once available.

## Required issue metadata

Define a stable machine-readable block for programme issues containing at least:

- programme phase;
- parent epic;
- lifecycle state (`blocked`, `ready`, `claimed`, `in_progress`, `review`, `merged`, `verified`, `released`, `human_evidence`, `superseded`);
- dependencies by issue number;
- blocking issues;
- expected ownership surfaces/files/globs if known;
- risk tier;
- required evidence layers;
- user journey / capability IDs;
- release gate impact;
- whether human/external evidence is required;
- whether the issue may be safely worked in parallel;
- next reconciliation checkpoint.

Do not create a second product/evidence authority. This metadata coordinates work and traceability only.

## Agent issue template

Every executable issue must contain these sections:

1. User outcome
2. Current evidence / known gap
3. In scope
4. Out of scope
5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
6. Canonical model / operations impact
7. UI/UX states
8. Persistence / recovery impact
9. Security / privacy impact
10. Accessibility / input impact
11. Performance impact
12. Tests and exact-head evidence
13. Acceptance criteria
14. Agent progress updates
15. ZEUS CTO reconciliation notes

## Progress-update protocol

While an issue is active, its agent must update the issue at meaningful checkpoints with:

- branch and head SHA;
- files/interfaces actually touched;
- assumptions changed after reading code;
- evidence run and result;
- blockers discovered;
- follow-up issue required, if any;
- whether the original scope remains valid.

The issue must not be marked complete merely because a PR was opened.

## Dependency rules

- A blocked issue must not be auto-selected by ZEUS.
- An issue whose dependency has changed materially must be re-preflighted before implementation continues.

- Research-only issues reserve no runtime files unless they become implementation lanes.

- [ ] A validator can parse programme issues and reject malformed executable issues.

- [ ] Dependencies and conflicts are surfaced before mutation begins.

- [ ] The master issue #367 and all newly created programme issues can be represented without losing required information.
- [ ] Tests cover malformed metadata, dependency cycles, stale state, duplicate ownership metadata and blocked-issue selection.
- [ ] Documentation states clearly that product truth still comes from code/ADRs/evidence, not issue metadata.

Once this lands, the ZEUS CTO reconciler should use this contract to refresh programme state and to create later-phase atomic issues only when their phase gate is ready.

## Problem

- required with WebGPU

- supported with limitations

- Windows
- macOS Apple Silicon

- Linux if in product scope

- rendering performance and feature parity under WebGL fallback
- accessibility and keyboard behaviour
- support/QA cost of OS-specific Firefox promises
- security implications of capability detection and GPU feature gating
- release-test burden

- implementing browser-specific fixes
- adding Firefox Android support
- changing unrelated browser policy

title: ARQFS-003: Add lossless semantic wall operations for reference-format projects
disposition: Execute/reconcile existing issue; preserve source acceptance.
routing_basis: explicit owner mapping
body:
## Problem

Reference-format `.arq` projects cannot safely use the workspace's current `WorkspaceOperation` wall edits.

`WorkspaceOperation` carries only drawn wall centreline geometry and ids. A canonical reference wall also requires semantic identity such as `levelId` and `typeId`, and existing walls can own or affect openings, doors, windows, rooms and other dependent model content. The current native save encoder writes only the flat `{ projectName, walls }` shape.

Therefore treating a rich reference project like the flat editable model would either invent missing semantics or silently discard canonical project content.

## Goal

Create a lossless semantic mutation path for walls in reference-format projects so the editor can make real native edits without flattening the model or guessing project semantics.

## Scope

- Define semantic wall create/update/delete operations against the canonical reference model.
- Carry required level and wall-type identity explicitly. Never infer these from unrelated UI labels.
- Define dependency policy for hosted openings, doors/windows, rooms and other affected content on wall delete or geometry change.
- Preserve untouched levels, wall types, rooms, openings, doors, windows, placed content, services, pathways, views and project metadata byte-semantically where possible and semantically always.
- Add a reference-model encoder/serializer that round-trips the typed canonical model rather than projecting it to the flat wall format.
- Integrate operations with undo/redo and `NativeProjectSession` without duplicating its write queue.
- Reopen published output in an independent worker and prove semantic equivalence for untouched content plus the intended edit.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Adding a wall requires explicit valid `levelId` and `typeId` and survives publish/reopen.
2. Moving/updating a wall preserves its semantic identity and all unrelated canonical content.
3. Deleting a wall follows an explicit tested dependency policy for hosted/dependent elements. No orphan references are written.
4. A rich project containing multiple levels, wall types, rooms, openings, doors, windows, placed content and views retains all untouched content after edit/publish/reopen.
5. Invalid or incomplete semantic edits are refused rather than guessed.
6. The workspace can switch #355's reference-project persistence route from refusal to this semantic mutation path once these guarantees are proven.

## Relationship

Follow-up to #355. #355 must remain non-destructive and may persist only the flat native model until this semantic path exists.

title: ARQFS-002: Persist live editor operations through native project sessions
disposition: Execute/reconcile existing issue; preserve source acceptance.
routing_basis: explicit owner mapping
body:
## Problem

The native project write path already exists in `NativeProjectSession.save()`, but the workspace editor does not call it.

Today `App.tsx` applies typed plan operations to in-memory walls and records edit/undo/redo activity only through the IndexedDB demo journal (`PLAN_PROJECT_ID = 'demo-project'`). When a writable native `.arq` project is open, the same edits therefore do not advance the native working copy even though publication/checkpoint infrastructure exists.

There is also a critical format boundary: `NativeProjectSession.save()` currently re-encodes the editable model as the flat `{ projectName, walls }` shape. A reference-format project can contain levels, wall types, rooms, openings, doors, windows, placed content and views. Sending a reference project through the flat encoder would silently discard that richer content. This issue must not introduce that data loss.

## Goal

Connect live editor persistence to native project sessions where the current editor model can be round-tripped without loss, while preserving the current demo/recovery journal when no native project is open and explicitly refusing destructive persistence for richer reference projects until semantic edit operations exist.

## Scope

- Add a single workspace persistence bridge for edit, undo and redo operations.
- For a writable flat native project (`snapshot.document === null`), route the resulting wall state plus the exact typed `WorkspaceOperation` through `NativeProjectSession.save()`.
- Use the existing native session queue. Do not invent a second native save queue.
- Keep the existing IndexedDB plan journal for the no-native-project/demo path.
- For reference-format native projects (`snapshot.document !== null`), do not call the flat native save path. Report the project as not safely editable/persistable by the current wall operation model rather than flattening it.
- Respect read-only native projects. Do not silently fall back to the demo journal and imply the project was persisted.
- Do not report `saved` until the selected persistence authority acknowledges the write.
- Surface native write failure as unsaved/failed state without discarding the editor's visible operation or poisoning later saves.
- Ensure undo/redo use the same persistence path as forward edits.
- Make close/publish semantics account for in-flight editor persistence through the session's existing queue.
- Add focused tests for routing, native edit, undo/redo, failure recovery, reference-format refusal and read-only behaviour.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Opening a writable flat `.arq`, drawing/removing walls, then publishing produces bytes whose reopened model contains those edits.
2. Undo and redo change both the visible plan state and the flat native working copy.
3. A native write failure leaves the UI in an honest unsaved state; a later successful write is still attempted and can recover the session.
4. A read-only native project cannot be presented as saved after an edit attempt.
5. A reference-format project can never be flattened by an editor persistence attempt. The bridge refuses that route until semantic wall operations can preserve levels/types/dependants.
6. With no native project open, the current IndexedDB recovery behaviour remains intact.
7. Tests cover the persistence bridge without duplicating `NativeProjectSession` queue logic.

## Follow-up boundary

Reference-format wall editing needs a semantic operation that carries at least level and wall-type identity and preserves/cascades hosted/dependent content correctly. That work is tracked separately and is a prerequisite to making rich reference projects natively editable.

This issue is intentionally narrower than file-handle write-back to the original user-selected file. It closes the safe editor-to-native-working-copy bridge first.

title: ARQFS-001: Make `.arq` open a byte-safe compatibility gate
disposition: Retain history; closure is not current release proof. Reuse verified implementation and recheck only affected evidence.
routing_basis: proposed category/title route; verify before execution
body:
## Problem

The file picker must not hand arbitrary or future `.arq` bytes to SQLite or the editor. A reader must distinguish malformed, incompatible and healthy files before authoring begins.

## Scope

- Wire `preflightArqfsBytes` into every file-open path.
- Validate SQLite header fields, page/file limits, ARQ application ID, frozen meta, schema and required feature flags.
- Return stable reason codes and route to editable, read-only, migration or blocked states.

## Acceptance criteria

- Truncated, oversized, wrong-ID, future-major, future-schema and unknown-required-feature fixtures never construct an editable session.
- Older same-major schemas offer copy-on-write migration.
- The UI shows a short actionable message plus a diagnostics affordance.
- No raw SQLite error or empty editor shell leaks to users.

Scenarios: S001–S017.

## Live implementation status (2026-07-24)

The storage-layer half of this issue has landed on `claude/arq-master-agent-execution-ir9re1` (commit `3d808d5`):

- `packages/arqfs/src/arqfs-preflight.ts` — raw SQLite header checks for journal mode, reserved bytes, payload fractions, application ID, and declared vs physical page count (truncation detection), each with a stable code (`ARQ_INVALID_JOURNAL_MODE`, `ARQ_INVALID_RESERVED_BYTES`, `ARQ_INVALID_PAYLOAD_FRACTIONS`, `ARQ_FILE_TRUNCATED`, `ARQ_PAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`).
- `packages/arqfs/src/arqfs-open.ts` — refuses future-major and future-schema files, requires numeric version metadata, and treats unreadable feature flags as structural failure rather than "no flags declared".

Evidence: `npx vitest run packages/arqfs --coverage=false` → 23 files / 121 tests pass against a real `better-sqlite3` binding.

### Remaining for this issue

The **UI half is not done**: no file-open path is wired to `preflightArqfsBytes` yet, and no user-facing message or diagnostics affordance exists. That work depends on UI-011 (file open / import UI) and is tracked there.

Dependencies: UI-011, UI-013.

title: reliability: import-export worker cancellation has a race with in-flight conversion
disposition: Retain history; closure is not current release proof. Reuse verified implementation and recheck only affected evidence.
routing_basis: proposed category/title route; verify before execution
body:
Fixed in d19d388.

**Bug (FP-019):** `workers/import-export-worker/src/handler.ts` adapters only check `AbortSignal.aborted` once, at the very start of `convert()`. If a `cancel` request arrived after that check but before `convert()` resolved, the handler would still post a final `'converted'`/`'failed'` message for a request the caller had already been told was `'cancelled'` — a real race, not hypothetical, since today's adapters do all their work inside one synchronous-looking `async` call with no later checkpoint.

**Fix:** added a `cancelledRequestIds: Set<string>` plus a `postFinal()` wrapper that silently drops any late `'converted'`/`'failed'` post for a requestId already reported as `'cancelled'`. Once a request is cancelled its outcome is permanently `'cancelled'`; anything settling afterward is dropped, not posted.

**Regression test:** new test in `handler.test.ts` uses a fake adapter whose `convert()` only resolves when the test explicitly releases it, so the cancel genuinely arrives mid-flight (not just asserting the code path exists). Asserts `post` is called exactly once, with `{ type: 'cancelled', requestId: 'r5' }`, and never with `'converted'` or `'failed'`.

Verified: `npx vitest run workers/import-export-worker` — 6/6 passing. `npx turbo run typecheck --filter=@arq/import-export-worker` — clean.

**ARQ-209** | Phase: File-system and instant architecture foundation

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/209-sync-implement-safe-rebase-and-conflict-classes.md`

## Resolution

Commit `998906e` adds `conflict-classification.ts` + `safe-rebase.ts`. Operations are described only by which entity IDs they wrote/deleted (not their full semantic type), keeping this package decoupled from `@arq/operations`/`@arq/arqscript` - a real, standard optimistic-concurrency conflict-detection pattern (compare touched-entity sets), not a placeholder.

`classifyConflict` distinguishes `concurrent-write` (both wrote the same entity - mergeable in principle) from the more severe `write-after-delete` (one deleted an entity the other wrote to). `computeSafeRebasePlan` classifies each client operation independently against the server operations since its `baseRevision` - a conflicted operation is reported explicitly with its conflict class and the specific conflicting server operation, never silently reapplied or dropped, matching "invalid operations leave committed state unchanged."

**Explicit scope boundary, documented rather than silently assumed away**: no transitive dependency-chain analysis between a client's own pending operations (e.g. operation B assumed operation A's effect, A conflicted, so B might now be unsafe too even though B itself touches nothing server-side changed) - that needs real operation semantics this generic module does not have.

**ARQ-237** | Epic: v3 execution readiness

## Resolution

Commit `2cd4ebb` adds `arqfs-defensive-open.ts`: `applyDefensiveOpenPolicy(driver, { readOnly })` sets `PRAGMA trusted_schema = OFF` (disables trusted-schema-only SQL functions/features a malicious file's embedded triggers/views/check-constraints could otherwise invoke), a bounded `busy_timeout` (5000ms, rather than indefinite blocking on lock contention), and `PRAGMA query_only = ON` for read-only opens (pairs with `resolveArqfsSafeModePlan`'s `openReadOnly`).

**ARQ-172** | Phase: Phase 8 | Epic: Native iPad | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-171

## Resolution

Commit `3389cc3` adds `hover-preview.ts` to `@arq/input-system`, building the actual hover-preview interaction on top of ARQ-171's confirmed `pointerover`-without-`pointerdown` capability.

- **Pencil, finger and keyboard roles are separated**: `createHoverPreviewTracker` only starts a hover session for a pointer `pointer-role.ts`'s `classifyPointerInputRole` reports as `'pencil'` — a `'touch'` or `'mouse'` `over` sample is correctly ignored (verified by test), matching blueprint section 13's assignment of "hover preview" to Apple Pencil specifically, not Finger or Keyboard/trackpad.
- **Native value compared with browser behaviour**: a second real-browser check (`hover-sequence-capability.html` + `run-hover-sequence-capability-check.mjs`, `pnpm benchmark:hover-sequence`) dispatched a full `over -> move -> move -> out` sequence (no `down`) for `pen`, `touch`, and `mouse` pointer types in real headless Chromium.
- **Honest, important finding recorded rather than glossed over**: all three pointer types produced an *identical* event sequence — the DOM's dispatch API does not restrict a hover sequence by `pointerType` at all. The Pencil-only restriction is entirely this repository's own application-level role check, not something the browser enforces. Separately, real touchscreens have no hardware hover/proximity sensing at all (a real finger physically cannot generate `pointerover` before contact the way a real Pencil can) — but confirming that physical difference needs real touch hardware, which this sandboxed environment does not have; only the synthetic-dispatch behavior was verified here. Documented explicitly in `docs/research/PENCIL-WEB-INPUT.md`, not hidden.
- A real contact (`pointerdown`) always ends the current hover-preview session for that pointer, matching how a real Pencil transitions from hovering to touching.

## Evidence

- 10 new tests (`hover-preview.test.ts`): session start/move/end, contact ending hover, touch/mouse correctly ignored, multiple concurrent pointers, and re-starting after a session ends.

## Resolution

Commit `0d7392c` adds a hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser to `@arq/arqscript`, turning ArqScript v0 source text into the AST ARQ-166 already defined:

- **`arqscript-lexer.ts`**: `tokenize` — strings, numbers, `length` tokens (a number with an immediate unit suffix, per `docs/ai/ARQSCRIPT-GRAMMAR.ebnf`'s `length = number, unit`), identifiers, punctuation. Throws `ArqScriptSyntaxError` (with a source position) on anything it cannot lex.
- **`arqscript-token-cursor.ts`**: a small shared cursor over the token stream (`expectPunct`/`expectIdent`/`expectString`/...).
- **`arqscript-length.ts`** / **`arqscript-value-parser.ts`**: unit-to-millimetre conversion, and the grammar's generic `value`/`point`/`array`/`property` productions, with typed accessors (`requireStringProperty`, `optionalLengthMmProperty`, `requirePointArrayProperty`, ...) used by every command parser.
- **`arqscript-parser.ts`**: `parseArqScript(source, scriptId)` — dispatches on each of the eleven statement keywords and delegates every command's required/optional field validation to its own `arqscript-command.ts` constructor (ARQ-166), so defaults and assumption messages live in exactly one place, not duplicated here.

- **"Output is a previewable typed operation"**: verified end-to-end — parsing the exact blueprint section 98 example script produces the expected `CreateLevel`/`CreateWall`/`PlaceDoor` commands with correct `operationType`s.
- **"Assumptions ... visible"**: parsing a wall block that omits `type`/`height` produces two assumption strings, retrievable via `collectAssumptions`.
- **Never throws**: every `ArqScriptSyntaxError` (bad syntax) or `RangeError` (semantically invalid data from a constructor, e.g. an empty host) is caught and converted to a well-formed `'rejected'` result carrying a source position — the same safe-failure boundary `@arq/dxf-adapter`'s `parseDxf` and `@arq/project-format`'s `importArchive` already use.
- **AI guardrail "No arbitrary code execution"** (`docs/ai/AI-GUARDRAILS.md`): holds trivially — this is a plain-text parser producing only AST data, with no `eval`/`Function`/dynamic dispatch anywhere.

- **`presence-state.ts`** (no Yjs dependency, pure data): `deriveInitials` (section 85's "participant initials"), `derivePresenceStatus` ('active'/'idle' only — see below), and `buildVisiblePresence`, which gates each remote participant's data into what a viewer is actually allowed to see — selection hidden unless permitted, cursor shown only in the same view, viewer's own entry excluded.
- **`presence-awareness.ts`**: wires that shape onto `y-protocols`' real `Awareness` class (`createPresenceAwareness`, `setLocalPresence`, `clearLocalPresence`, `readPresenceStates`, `syncAwarenessUpdate` for relaying real encoded updates between instances) plus `parsePresenceState`, a defensive parser for remote (untrusted) state.

Verified directly: two independently-set participants' states never interfere (`presence-awareness.test.ts`).
- **"Offline" has no synthetic status value**: it's simply a participant's absence from the awareness map once Awareness removes them — inventing a fake `'offline'` enum member with no real signal behind it was rejected as exactly the kind of fabrication this backlog avoids.
- **"Server-side permissions are enforced"**: honestly scoped — no permission system or backend exists yet (`security/THREAT-MODEL.md`: "No permission system is implemented yet"). `isSelectionPermitted` is a caller-supplied predicate; this issue's real, tested contribution is that the client-side gate correctly hides selection whenever it says no, not that server-side enforcement exists — recorded explicitly in both the code doc comments and the package README rather than silently implied as done.

- **Real, measured limitation documented rather than hidden**: on malformed/invalid content, `web-ifc`'s own `OpenModel` can take anywhere from ~1 to over 30 real seconds before throwing (a characteristic of the library's own internal error handling, confirmed by direct measurement in this sandbox) — recorded in both `ifc-viewer.ts`'s doc comment and the package README as a reason untrusted IFC content needs an outer size/timeout gate before reaching this module (same category as ARQ-157's archive limits), tracked as follow-up rather than silently ignored.
- A module-level singleton (`getIfcApi`) avoids re-paying `web-ifc`'s real WASM initialization cost on every call, with a failed initialization not cached (so a transient failure doesn't permanently wedge the module).

## Evidence

- 6 tests in `ifc-viewer.test.ts`: reads a realistic sample's spatial structure + building elements with correct names/global IDs; produces a correct support report (7 of 8 lines preserved, 1 `IFCFURNISHINGELEMENT` correctly counted as unsupported); rejects a header-less file, empty content, and a truncated header, all without throwing; produces an empty-but-valid result for a well-formed file with no recognized entities. Two tests use a generous 60s timeout with a comment explaining the measured real-world variance in `web-ifc`'s own error path.
- Full workspace suite: 971/971 passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean across all packages (`turbo run typecheck`, 26/26). Prettier clean on every file this change touches.

Commit `09043fc` adds `packages/project-format/src/complexity-limits.ts` and wires it into `archive.ts`'s `importArchive` (ARQ-079):

- **File size**: `MAX_ARCHIVE_TOTAL_BYTES` (1 GiB) caps the sum of every archive entry's byte length, on top of the existing per-entry `MAX_ENTRY_BYTES` cap (500 MiB) — closes the gap where several near-per-entry-cap entries could otherwise sum to an unbounded total.

Traversal is iterative (explicit stack, not recursion) so checking a hostile deeply-nested payload cannot itself overflow the call stack.
- Applied to `model.json` (required — exceeding either limit rejects the whole archive) and to `views.json`/`sheets.json`/`operations.ndjson` (optional-cache-like — exceeding either limit is reported via `corruptOptionalPaths`, same fail-safe-not-fatal handling as any other corrupt optional section, per `archive.ts`'s existing design).

- `complexity-limits.test.ts` (8 tests): sums entry bytes correctly; does not flag a realistic benchmark-scale BIM model (150 walls/60 rooms); flags node-count and depth overruns with the correct reason string; never throws (and correctly flags) a 200,000-deep nested value, proving the iterative traversal doesn't stack-overflow; ignores primitives.

Implemented in commit 1977285 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`createVisibilityState`/`hideElements`/`showElements`/`isolateElements`/`exitIsolate`/`effectiveHiddenSet` (`packages/plan-renderer/src/visibility-state.ts`) - section 62's "First 3D features" lists "hide; isolate" alongside orbit/pan/zoom/fit (ARQ-127) and shared selection (ARQ-128). The rendering half of both (an invisible element / an omitted primitive) already exists - `resolveStyleToken`/`buildPlanScene` (ARQ-119) and `applySharedSelection` (ARQ-128) both already take a `hidden` set as input. What was left for this issue is computing that set from "hide this"/"isolate this"/"exit isolate" user intent - genuinely shared 2D/3D state, so it lives alongside `plan-scene.ts`'s other shared-renderer concepts.

Hide and isolate are kept as two separate, composable concepts on purpose: `hidden` is the user's explicit, persistent "don't show this" set - it survives isolating and un-isolating. `isolated` is a temporary overlay that can be entered and exited without disturbing `hidden` - exiting isolate restores exactly the hide state from before isolating, not an empty one. This matches how "isolate" behaves in every mainstream 3D/CAD viewer: hiding a reference layer, then isolating a room to work on it, then exiting isolate, should not silently bring the reference layer back.

`effectiveHiddenSet` is the one function a renderer actually needs: given the full universe of element ids (needed only to know what "everything else" means while isolating), it folds `hidden` and `isolated` into the single hidden-set shape `resolveStyleToken`/`applySharedSelection` already expect.

**What was built**

`orbitBy`/`panBy`/`zoomBy`/`fitBoundingSphere`/`applyOrbitCameraState`/`createOrbitingCamera` (`packages/model-renderer/src/orbit-camera.ts`) - blueprint section 62's "orbit; pan; zoom; fit selection; fit project," the interaction half of the 3D camera built on ARQ-126's plain `THREE.OrthographicCamera` construction.

`OrbitCameraState` is plain data (spherical coordinates around a target, plus the orthographic `viewSize`) - the same "pure state, apply to a real object at the edge" split `viewport-controller.ts` (ARQ-033) already uses for the 2D viewport, so `orbitBy`/`panBy`/`zoomBy`/`fitBoundingSphere` are all independently-testable pure functions; `applyOrbitCameraState` is the one function that actually touches a `THREE.OrthographicCamera`.

For an orthographic camera, distance from the target never changes apparent scale - only `viewSize` does, so `zoomBy` changes `viewSize`, not distance, with the same sign convention as `viewport-controller.ts`'s `zoomAtScreenPoint` (factor > 1 zooms in), keeping the 2D and 3D cameras consistent.

`fitBoundingSphere` is the 3D analogue of `fitToBounds`: a bounding sphere (centre + radius) is the simplest volume that already covers an axis-aligned box under an arbitrary orbit angle, and `viewSize` is sized to fit the sphere in whichever screen dimension needs more room, accounting for aspect ratio.

`panBy` takes an already-world-space delta rather than a screen-space one - converting a screen drag to world space needs the camera's current right/up vectors, a renderer/input concern this pure-state module leaves to its caller, the same pattern `zoom-to-room-gap.ts` and `snap-glyph-rendering.ts` already establish.

`generateWallOpeningMeshes` (`packages/geometry-3d/src/wall-opening-meshes.ts`) - blueprint section 39's "opening subtraction for supported primitives." **What was built**

`LineWeight` (hairline through heavy) and `lineWeightToDevicePixels`/`snapStrokeCenter` (`packages/plan-renderer/src/line-weight.ts`) - a renderer-independent way to keep technical linework crisp and visually hierarchical across zoom and device pixel ratio, the same "stable" quality a drafter expects from any CAD tool.

Each tier's canonical CSS-pixel width is chosen so the hierarchy stays visually distinct even at the lowest supported devicePixelRatio (1); `lineWeightToDevicePixels` floors at 1 device pixel only to protect against a devicePixelRatio below 1. `snapStrokeCenter` implements the standard canvas crisp-line technique (odd-device-pixel-width strokes snap to a half-pixel boundary, even widths to a whole-pixel boundary) so a renderer backend can avoid the blur a non-pixel-aligned stroke produces.

Implemented in commit 5af1686 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

- `pointInPolygon` (`point-in-polygon.ts`): a supporting primitive blueprint section 39 lists as a geometry-2d responsibility that no earlier issue implemented. Standard even-odd ray-casting, with an explicit boundary check first (a point exactly on an edge, within tolerance, always counts as inside).
- `traceRoomBoundary` (`room-boundary-graph.ts`): given a set of plain segments (generic over a caller-supplied edge id) and a seed point, finds the smallest enclosed polygon containing it - blueprint section 49's "click within an enclosed boundary; calculate polygon". Builds a half-edge graph (vertices merged within tolerance via `pointsAreCoincident`, ARQ-081), then enumerates every bounded face of the resulting planar subdivision using the standard "next = smallest clockwise turn from the reversed incoming edge" DCEL face-finding technique - this correctly splits a T-junction into its two smaller enclosed faces rather than tracing the whole outer perimeter, verified by a dedicated test. The one negative-signed-area face (the unbounded outer face) is excluded; among the rest, `pointInPolygon` finds which contain the seed, and the smallest by area is returned.

Deliberately takes centerlines, not wall face lines - this module doesn't know or care what a segment's endpoints represent, so a caller can pass wall face lines (ARQ-093) instead for a more precisely bounded result, consistent with ADR-0007's "purpose-built, start simple" direction.

**Known, documented limitation**: "room containing island" (section 42) - a polygon with a hole - is a multi-ring concept neither `pointInPolygon` nor `polygon-area.ts` model, so it's not handled by this first cut.

- `seedPoint`/`calculatedBoundary` use geometry-2d's `WorldPoint` rather than a naked `{x,y}`. Unlike Wall/Door/Window, Room has no RoomType - the blueprint's own Room interface has no `typeId` field and section 49 never describes a reusable room type a Room instance inherits defaults from - so there is no type-instance `PropertyState` split to implement. "Stable IDs / type-instance behaviour preserved" is upheld by `RoomId` never changing across a Room's own property updates, and by not fabricating an inheritance relationship the blueprint doesn't describe.

`createRoom` accepts `boundaryElementIds`/`calculatedBoundary`/`calculatedArea`/`status` as given rather than computing them - the boundary graph walk (ARQ-111), area calculation (ARQ-114), and "click within an enclosed boundary" placement workflow (ARQ-112) are all separate, later issues. `createCandidateCycler<TId>()`: `begin(ids)` starts (or restarts) cycling over a fresh candidate stack and returns the top-priority id; `cycleNext()` advances to the next candidate underneath, wrapping around after the last; `current()`/`reset()` round it out. A fresh click always calls `begin()` again, resetting back to the top candidate - cycling only applies to repeated Tab presses against the same click.

Also added `pickAllAt` to `hit-test.ts` (ARQ-039) - like `pickAt` but returns every matching candidate's id in priority order, which is what the cycler needs to know the full stack under the pointer (not just the winner).

**Escape/Enter**: Escape stops cycling and clears the candidate stack (the caller also clears the actual selection, mirroring ARQ-040's point-selection escape). Enter has no defined behaviour - no preview/commit step exists here, same rationale as point/region selection.

Verified with 7 tests (vitest): top-candidate-first, empty-stack handling, wrap-around cycling, reset-on-fresh-click, and explicit `reset()`. Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (63 tests across 10 files) passes.

Implemented alongside ARQ-041 in `packages/editor-shell/src/region-selection.ts` (commit d4d0cc2, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

`selectInRegion(candidates, region, 'crossing')` keeps any candidate for which `intersectsRegion(region)` is true (any overlap counts, not just full containment).

Important, explicitly documented and tested honesty note: for the only candidate shape implemented so far (`createPointRegionTestable`, a zero-area point), window and crossing selection are necessarily identical - a point either lies inside the rectangle or it doesn't, there is no partial-overlap case for something with no extent. The two modes can only diverge once a candidate with real extent exists (e.g. a line that crosses a rectangle edge without either endpoint being inside it) - that depends on a line/wall candidate shape, which needs a document/scene model that doesn't exist yet in this repo (`packages/bim-core` is still an empty scaffold - the same gap noted when ARQ-034 closed). This is not a shortcut or a missed distinction; it's the correct behavior given what candidate shapes currently exist, and is asserted directly in the test suite.

Which direction a drag went (left-to-right = window, right-to-left = crossing, the usual CAD convention) is left to the caller - this module only answers "given a mode, which candidates match", not which mode a given drag implies.

Covered by the same 5 tests as ARQ-041 (one specifically asserts the window/crossing equivalence for point candidates). Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (56 tests across 9 files) passes.

`createCommandLifecycle()` implements all 8 documented states (Idle, Armed, Previewing, Awaiting input, Validating, Committed, Failed safely, Cancelled) as a closure-based state machine (`arm`, `beginPreview`, `editField`, `placeSegment`, `commit`, `escape`, `reset`), consistent with the input-system trackers from ARQ-035/036/037.

**Escape behaviour**: graduated three tiers exactly as specced - clears a pending field edit first; if none, cancels (pops) the most recently placed segment; if no field or segments remain, exits the tool to Cancelled.

- `comboKeyFor(sample)`: canonicalizes a key sample into a fixed-order combo string (e.g. `ctrl+shift+z`), so lookups are independent of the order modifiers are reported in.
- `createKeyboardShortcutRegistry()`: `register`/`unregister` bindings from a combo string to a command id, and `dispatch(sample)` resolving a sample to `{type: 'cancel'}`, `{type: 'commit'}`, `{type: 'shortcut', commandId}`, or `{type: 'unhandled', combo}`.

Implemented in `packages/input-system/src/touch-gesture.ts` (commit 71fec77, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

`createTwoFingerGestureTracker()` - recognizes two-finger pinch/pan from a per-frame set of active touch points. Tracks the two lowest-id touches (a third simultaneous contact is ignored rather than restarting the gesture), and emits `pinch-start`, then `pinch-move` (centroid pan delta + spread-ratio zoom factor + anchor point) each frame, then `pinch-end` when either tracked finger lifts. The output shape (`panDxScreen`/`panDyScreen`/`zoomFactor`/`anchorX`/`anchorY`) is designed to feed directly into `@arq/editor-shell`'s `panByScreenDelta` and `zoomAtScreenPoint` from ARQ-033. DOM-free by design (plain `{id, x, y}` samples, not `TouchEvent`/`TouchList`).

A lone touch point is intentionally not handled here - it's just a pointer, so it goes through `pointer-gesture.ts`'s tracker (ARQ-035) like mouse and pen input.

Verified with 6 tests (vitest), all passing: no-op on 0/1 touches, pinch-start/move/end lifecycle, correct centroid-pan and spread-ratio-zoom arithmetic, ignoring a third finger, and restarting cleanly after a gesture ends. Package typechecks clean.

`createPointerGestureTracker(dragThresholdPx?)` - a single-pointer gesture state machine turning raw down/move/up/cancel samples into `tap` / `drag-start` / `drag-move` / `drag-end` / `cancel` intents, with a configurable movement threshold before a gesture counts as a drag. title: editor: implement pan and zoom
disposition: Retain history; closure is not current release proof. Reuse verified implementation and recheck only affected evidence.

body:
Implemented in `packages/editor-shell/src/viewport-controller.ts` (commit 3ec41c4, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`), built on ARQ-032's `@arq/geometry-2d` primitives:

- `panByScreenDelta(viewport, dxScreen, dyScreen)`: grab-and-drag pan - content follows the drag gesture, so the world centre moves opposite-signed in x and same-signed in y (screen y-down vs world y-up).
- `zoomAtScreenPoint(viewport, anchorScreen, factor)`: zoom-under-cursor - the world point currently under `anchorScreen` stays visually fixed after zooming, not zoom-toward-viewport-centre. Throws `RangeError` on a non-positive/non-finite factor. Zoom is clamped to `[MIN_PIXELS_PER_UNIT, MAX_PIXELS_PER_UNIT]` (0.01 to 10,000).
- `fitToBounds(bounds, screenWidth, screenHeight, marginPx)`: "fit to selection/view" - centres and scales a world-space bounding box to fit on screen with a margin, picking the more constraining axis.

Deliberately framework- and input-library-agnostic (pure functions over `Viewport` state) since no frontend framework is locked in yet (`open-source/TECHNOLOGY-MATRIX.csv`) and wiring actual pointer/wheel/touch events to these functions is a separate, later issue (ARQ-035/036/037, input abstractions).

Verified with 10 tests (vitest + fast-check), all passing: pan direction/zoom-scaling correctness, a property-based test that the zoom anchor point lands back on the same screen pixel across arbitrary anchors and zoom factors, min/max zoom clamping, invalid-factor rejection, and fitToBounds centering/axis-selection/degenerate-box handling. Both `@arq/geometry-2d` and `@arq/editor-shell` typecheck clean (`tsc --noEmit`).

body:
Implemented in `packages/geometry-2d/src/coordinate-system.ts` (commit 3ec41c4, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

- `WorldPoint` / `ScreenPoint`: structurally distinct branded types (nominal typing via a `Brand<T, N>` helper) so a screen coordinate can never be silently substituted for a world coordinate without going through an explicit conversion.
- `Viewport`: `{ center, pixelsPerUnit, screenWidth, screenHeight }` - the camera/view transform.
- `worldToScreen` / `screenToWorld`: the two conversion functions, correctly handling the world-is-y-up vs screen-is-y-down flip.

Verified with 5 real tests (vitest + fast-check property-based testing), all passing:
1. Property-based round-trip (`screenToWorld(worldToScreen(p)) === p`) across arbitrary viewports and points.
2. Viewport centre renders to screen middle.
3. Y-flip behaves correctly (world "up" renders to a smaller screen-y).
4. 2x zoom doubles on-screen distance between two world points.
5. Type-level test (`@ts-expect-error`) proving a `ScreenPoint` is not assignable where a `WorldPoint` is expected.

Both note: `docs/adr/0004-units-and-numeric-representation.md` is still "Research required" (mm vs m, fixed vs floating point is not decided). This module uses plain floating-point numbers as a provisional, easily-swappable choice consistent with `contracts/model.ts`'s existing `Point2` - not a claim that ADR-0004 is resolved.

**What was built**

`packages/design-system/src/shell/model-panel-state.ts` + `model-panel.tsx`, reviewed against blueprint section 12 > "Model panel." A generic `ModelPanelNode` tree (site/building/levels/views/sheets/schedules/imports/warnings all fit as node types — kept domain-agnostic, not importing `@arq/bim-core`'s concrete types, the same layering `@arq/plan-renderer`'s `PlanPrimitive<TId>` already established).

body:
Implemented in commit `5df8916` on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

`scripts/check-dependency-licences.mjs` runs `pnpm licenses list --json` (already available - pnpm ships it, so no new dependency was added for this) against the allow-list in the new `docs/product/DEPENDENCY-AND-LICENCE-POLICY.md` (ARQ-003), fails non-zero if any package's licence is outside the allow-list or the documented reviewed-exceptions, and writes `dependency-sbom.json` (name/version/licence for every installed package - a minimal software bill of materials) as a build artifact.

Wired into CI as the new `dependency-licence-scan` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, uploading the SBOM as a workflow artifact on every run.

**Evidence**: ran against the real, current 195-package dependency tree - correctly identified and required handling for both compound-licence forms actually present (`(MIT OR WTFPL)`-style choices and `(MIT AND Zlib)`-style simultaneous licences), passes clean today with zero disallowed licences. `pnpm run check:dependency-licences` reproduces this locally.
